meta.source: Federal minimum UEF (10 CFR 430.32(d)); ENERGY STAR Version 5.0 criteria; Rheem Performance spec sheets (standard gas and electric tanks); ENERGY STAR certified list (heat pump and gas tankless)
meta.notes: Uniform Energy Factor (UEF) is the DOE efficiency rating printed on the EnergyGuide label: hot water energy delivered ÷ energy used in the 24-hour test. Defaults are typical values for each type; your unit's own UEF (on its label or spec sheet) always beats a default. Electric tankless units are not ENERGY STAR certified, so the federal minimum is used as a conservative default. Federal minimums below are the current rules for units made before May 6, 2029, for the medium and high draw patterns that most 40 to 50 gallon tanks are rated under (Vr = rated storage volume in gallons).

gas_tank.label: Gas tank (standard vent)
gas_tank.source: Rheem Performance atmospheric gas spec sheet (.58 to .66 UEF); build:data takes low / median / high of the 40 and 50 gallon models

gas_tank_high_efficiency.label: Gas tank (high efficiency, ENERGY STAR)
gas_tank_high_efficiency.source: ENERGY STAR criteria (UEF ≥ 0.81 medium draw, ≥ 0.86 high draw, tanks up to 55 gallons); typical = median of certified gas storage models

electric_tank.label: Electric tank
electric_tank.source: Rheem Performance electric spec sheets; build:data takes low / median / high of the 40 and 50 gallon models

heat_pump.label: Heat pump (hybrid), 240 V
heat_pump.source: ENERGY STAR criteria (integrated heat pump UEF ≥ 3.30) and certified list

gas_tankless.label: Gas tankless
gas_tankless.source: Federal minimum 0.81 (non-condensing units can be rated near it); ENERGY STAR minimum 0.95; certified models range 0.95 to 0.98 (median 0.95)

electric_tankless.label: Electric tankless
electric_tankless.source: Rheem RTEX whole-house models (18 to 36 kW), spec sheet TKE-101 Rev. 8 (04/24): UEF 0.94, 0.93, 0.93 and 0.94; typical = their median. Federal minimum for instantaneous electric water heaters: 0.91 (very small to medium draw), 0.92 (high draw). Audit F-13, 2026-11-14: the old default was the federal minimum, below the electric tank's 0.93.

federalMinimums.source: 10 CFR 430.32(d)(1): minimum UEF = intercept − perGallon × Vr
federalMinimums.electricResistanceMaxGallonsNote: Above 55 gallons rated volume, the federal minimum UEF for electric storage tanks (about 2.1 and up) can only be met by a heat pump water heater, so standard electric resistance tanks stop at 55 gallons.

doe2029.rule: Energy conservation standards for consumer water heaters, final rule
quotes: Compliance with the new and amended standards established for consumer water heaters in this final rule is required on and after May 6, 2029.
These standards apply to all products listed in Table I.1 and manufactured in, or imported into, the United States starting on May 6, 2029.
for certain classes of electric storage water heaters the adopted standards are currently only met through use of heat pump technology
at the adopted standard level, the minimum efficiency requirement for small electric storage water heaters is still achievable with electric resistance heating technology

the new standards for electric storage water heaters with capacities greater than or equal to 20 gallons and less than or equal to 55 gallons are met through the use of heat pump technology, while the standards for small electric storage water heaters (capacities greater than or equal to 20 gallons and less than or equal to 35 gallons) can be met by electric resistance heating technology
doe2029.smallClassDefinition: electric storage water heaters with an effective storage volume of 20 gallons up to 35 gallons and a first hour rating below 51 gallons (very small and low draw patterns)
